critic_rerun.summary:
s2a01 passes at 8.0 against the 7.5 line, with nothing fatal. Three must-fix items, all one-clause staging fixes in the action text; no dialogue changes. I worked by hand count and Grep only: no shell, no JSON parser, no script.

**Files**
- Script: <repo>/content/series2/episodes/s2a01/script.hi.json (parity: script.en.json in the same folder)
- S2 saves this review word for word into <repo>/content/series2/episodes/s2a01/review-notes.json under "critic". It must keep the existing "continuity" and "writer_response" sections, and replace the old tool-gap "pass/score/must_fix/summary", which reviewed nothing.

**Verdict:** pass, round 1, score 8.0. Sub-scores: hook 8, stakes 7.5, choice n/a, branch_distinct 9, cliffhanger 8, hinglish 8.5, performability 7.5, length 7.5, continuity 8.

**Checks run (all by hand or Grep)**
- **JSON:** not parsed. Pattern searches on both files found no comma before ] or }, no missing comma at a line break, no stray double quotes (only array lines have more than 4 quotes) and no backslashes.
- **Ids:** all 4 speaker ids and all 4 location ids exist in bible.json.
- **Tags:** emotion_tags matches the inline tag on 27 of 27 lines, one tag each, in hi and in en.
- **Durations:** 103.7 s spoken, plus 19.1 s of silence (each of the 11 beats has a silent_position), plus 14 speaker changes at 0.3 s (4.2 s), gives 127.0, which equals target_total_seconds. The en file sums the same way to its 122.1.
- **Line count:** 27.
- **Characters:** 962 dialogue code points by hand, tags excluded. The nukta is stored as a combining mark (U+093C on 15 lines, no precomposed U+0958-095F), so the writer's 962 stands with no correction. Per line, 8.1 to 9.8 characters a second; none over 12; mean 9.3.
- **hi/en parity:** same beat ids (b1 to b11), line ids (l01 to l27), speakers, silent_seconds and on_screen.
- **Lead on screen:** Nandini is in 11 of 11 beats.
- **Bookish forms:** no यह/वह and none of किंतु, परंतु, अतः, कृपया, हेतु, तथा in the dialogue. The one यह/वह hit is in writer_notes.
- **Shot limits on targets:** b1 shot 1 is 8.6 s, b9 shot 1 is 11.6 s, b9 shot 2 is 8.7 s and b6 shot 3 is 7.4 s.
- **Length estimate:** at the 8.4 characters a second measured on the photoreal proof, about 138 s, inside D-019's 150 s ceiling.

**Decisions met:** D-016 directions 5 (b9 speakers), 11 (l02/l03 as two lines), 14 (two sheet faces at most per frame; Pushpa as a silhouette, a back or hands) and 19 (no helmet from b8; ov_shield in b10). 'सुबह दस बजे' is correctly said after midnight. No bare साहब, and nobody calls Nirala Inspector. D-004 directions 4 to 6 hold: the ending is spoken, both overlays have spoken cover, and the revolver is only seen in profile.

**Glimpse A (ends on l08): PASS.** It uses b1 (the cuffs image and l03), b4 shot 3 (the door closing, with l06 optional), b5 (clock insert and l07) and b6 shot 1 (headlights, her hand up, l08). Checked against must_not_reveal, it does not show:
- the slip or the signature (the slip enters in shot 2, after l08);
- 'काग़ज़ पूरे हैं';
- the tail-lights or 'मैंने जाने दिया';
- 'FIR लिखिए' or the ten o'clock idea;
- the shut door or l27;
- anyone signing, the walk, or the key and the register;
- the b8 inference;
- the DSP, any s2a02 or s2a03 image, or the transfer.

The gate arm is still down in the last frame, so the truck has not passed.

**Why it scores well**
- The cuffs land on frame one, inside the moment the vote chose.
- A's cost (the truck passing) is on screen by about 44 s.
- The new deadline has a spoken mechanism (l19, l20).
- The ending is a spoken refusal, and s2a02 opens inside it.

- Each character speaks in their own register.

**Why it does not score higher**
- The delivery stays narrow: almost every line is quiet or calm.
- The b8 inference leans on the viewer doing the time arithmetic.
- Three staging contradictions, which are the must-fix items.
